o1.biggest_strength: Clearly frames the break-even math on why cutting the commission to 20% is dangerous, showing it only takes a 12.5% drop to wipe out the savings.
o1.biggest_mistake: Raises the commission rate to 40% for the top tier, which arguably goes against the owner's note to reward the top 20 'without raising cost across the board'.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the commission at 30% for all tiers to strictly follow the budget constraints, and provide more accurate first-year cohort cost modelling for the window extension.

o2.biggest_strength: Breathtakingly accurate reverse-engineering of the true number of creator-sent customers, paired with the brilliant, fresh idea of using the signup survey for attribution.
o2.biggest_mistake: None; this is a spectacular, deeply reasoned piece of work that perfectly grasps e-commerce cohort dynamics.

reason: While both models correctly caught the broken promise of retroactive cuts and the cash-flow pull-forward of faster payouts, Output 2 went above and beyond. It flawlessly reverse-engineered the cohort size from the revenue numbers to project precise year-one costs, included strict FTC guidelines, and offered a highly original survey attribution workaround.
